CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: add sysctl entry to allow dev mode-only syscalls Chromium OS defines a few alt-syscall tables to whitelist certain system calls in a container. There are scenarios when we would like to expose more system calls to a container, but only do so when the host system is in the developer mode. To allow that, this CL adds a sysctl entry 'kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls', which can be controlled by a privileged system service. The system service decides whether developer mode-only system calls are allowed by performing checks on the current mode and any applied device policies (see CL:421087 and CL:425454) BUG=b:33450588 TEST=Verify that the added sysctl entry '/proc/sys/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls' exists and can only be written by root. Change-Id: Id7c61b8c13de22c5b0f70b3ebb165e35418d28a2 Signed-off-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425861 Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: whitelist perf_event_open for Android Android provides a native profiling tool called simpleperf, which uses the perf_event_open system call exposed by the Linux kernel. Android CTS has a CtsSimpleperfTestCases module that tests various simpleperf usage. To allow simpleperf and CtsSimpleperfTestCases running under the Android container on ChromeOS, this CL whitelists the perf_event_open system call in the alt-syscall table for Android only when we allow developer mode-only system calls, which is controlled by the `kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls` sysctl entry. BUG=b:33450588 TEST=Tested the following on samus-cheets: - Set /proc/fs/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls to 1, verify that all CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests pass. - Set /proc/fs/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls to 0, verify that those CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests calling perf_event_open fail. Change-Id: Ie94e85f4b48fce4886597f0e49a125b94b36ca18 Signed-off-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/421087 Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>

This CL modifies the ui-pre-start job to update that sysctl entry, when exists, under developer mode. UPSTREAM: KEYS: Fix short sprintf buffer in /proc/keys show function This fixes CVE-2016-7042. Fix a short sprintf buffer in proc_keys_show(). If the gcc stack protector is turned on, this can cause a panic due to stack corruption. The problem is that xbuf[] is not big enough to hold a 64-bit timeout rendered as weeks: (gdb) p 0xffffffffffffffffULL/(60*60*24*7) $2 = 30500568904943 That's 14 chars plus NUL, not 11 chars plus NUL. Expand the buffer to 16 chars. I think the unpatched code apparently works if the stack-protector is not enabled because on a 32-bit machine the buffer won't be overflowed and on a 64-bit machine there's a 64-bit aligned pointer at one side and an int that isn't checked again on the other side. The panic incurred looks something like: Kernel panic - not syncing: stack-protector: Kernel stack is corrupted in: ffffffff81352ebe CPU: 0 PID: 1692 Comm: reproducer Not tainted 4.7.2-201.fc24.x86_64 #1 Hardware name: Red Hat KVM, BIOS 0.5.1 01/01/2011 0000000000000086 00000000fbbd2679 ffff8800a044bc00 ffffffff813d941f ffffffff81a28d58 ffff8800a044bc98 ffff8800a044bc88 ffffffff811b2cb6 ffff880000000010 ffff8800a044bc98 ffff8800a044bc30 00000000fbbd2679 Call Trace: [<ffffffff813d941f>] dump_stack+0x63/0x84 [<ffffffff811b2cb6>] panic+0xde/0x22a [<ffffffff81352ebe>] ? proc_keys_show+0x3ce/0x3d0 [<ffffffff8109f7f9>] __stack_chk_fail+0x19/0x30 [<ffffffff81352ebe>] proc_keys_show+0x3ce/0x3d0 [<ffffffff81350410>] ? key_validate+0x50/0x50 [<ffffffff8134db30>] ? key_default_cmp+0x20/0x20 [<ffffffff8126b31c>] seq_read+0x2cc/0x390 [<ffffffff812b6b12>] proc_reg_read+0x42/0x70 [<ffffffff81244fc7>] __vfs_read+0x37/0x150 [<ffffffff81357020>] ? security_file_permission+0xa0/0xc0 [<ffffffff81246156>] vfs_read+0x96/0x130 [<ffffffff81247635>] SyS_read+0x55/0xc0 [<ffffffff817eb872>] entry_SYSCALL_64_fastpath+0x1a/0xa4 Reported-by: Ondrej Kozina <okozina@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com> Tested-by: Ondrej Kozina <okozina@redhat.com> cc: stable@vger.kernel.org Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.l.morris@oracle.com> (cherry picked from commit 03dab869b7b239c4e013ec82aea22e181e441cfc) BUG=b:33006021 TEST=kernel compiles Change-Id: Id945e0d89cb53a35eb6add597681fdb3ad045de8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/413000 Commit-Ready: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Tested-by: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit f707658635bb9d9887e213b58da9c263c08a98c8) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/426092 Commit-Ready: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Tested-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

This means that a new dump could have started in the time being and we'll end up freeing their skb instead of ours. This patch saves the skb and module before we unlock so we free the right memory. BACKPORT: kvm: nVMX: Allow L1 to intercept software exceptions (#BP and #OF) When L2 exits to L0 due to "exception or NMI", software exceptions (#BP and #OF) for which L1 has requested an intercept should be handled by L1 rather than L0. Previously, only hardware exceptions were forwarded to L1. UPSTREAM: isofs: Fix infinite looping over CE entries Rock Ridge extensions define so called Continuation Entries (CE) which define where is further space with Rock Ridge data. Corrupted isofs image can contain arbitrarily long chain of these, including a one containing loop and thus causing kernel to end in an infinite loop when traversing these entries. Limit the traversal to 32 entries which should be more than enough space to store all the Rock Ridge data. UPSTREAM: ring-buffer: Prevent overflow of size in ring_buffer_resize() If the size passed to ring_buffer_resize() is greater than MAX_LONG - BUF_PAGE_SIZE then the DIV_ROUND_UP() will return zero. Here's the details: # echo 18014398509481980 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/buffer_size_kb tracing_entries_write() processes this and converts kb to bytes. 18014398509481980 << 10 = 18446744073709547520 and this is passed to ring_buffer_resize() as unsigned long size. size = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE); Where DIV_ROUND_UP(a, b) is (a + b - 1)/b BUF_PAGE_SIZE is 4080 and here 18446744073709547520 + 4080 - 1 = 18446744073709551599 where 18446744073709551599 is still smaller than 2^64 2^64 - 18446744073709551599 = 17 But now 18446744073709551599 / 4080 = 4521260802379792 and size = size * 4080 = 18446744073709551360 This is checked to make sure its still greater than 2 * 4080, which it is. Then we convert to the number of buffer pages needed. nr_page = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE) but this time size is 18446744073709551360 and 2^64 - (18446744073709551360 + 4080 - 1) = -3823 Thus it overflows and the resulting number is less than 4080, which makes 3823 / 4080 = 0 an nr_pages is set to this. As we already checked against the minimum that nr_pages may be, this causes the logic to fail as well, and we crash the kernel. There's no reason to have the two DIV_ROUND_UP() (that's just result of historical code changes), clean up the code and fix this bug. BUG=chromium:679490 TEST=Build and run basic tests Change-Id: Id1952e43fd481f680999ff0ec409973f38136258 Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.5+ Fixes: 83f40318dab00 ("ring-buffer: Make removal of ring buffer pages atomic") Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org> Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 59643d1535eb) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/426097 Reviewed-by: Bernie Thompson <bhthompson@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: mm: avoid setting up anonymous pages into file mapping Reading page fault handler code I've noticed that under right circumstances kernel would map anonymous pages into file mappings: if the VMA doesn't have vm_ops->fault() and the VMA wasn't fully populated on ->mmap(), kernel would handle page fault to not populated pte with do_anonymous_page(). Let's change page fault handler to use do_anonymous_page() only on anonymous VMA (->vm_ops == NULL) and make sure that the VMA is not shared. For file mappings without vm_ops->fault() or shred VMA without vm_ops, page fault on pte_none() entry would lead to SIGBUS. UPSTREAM: KEYS: Fix short sprintf buffer in /proc/keys show function This fixes CVE-2016-7042. Fix a short sprintf buffer in proc_keys_show(). If the gcc stack protector is turned on, this can cause a panic due to stack corruption. The problem is that xbuf[] is not big enough to hold a 64-bit timeout rendered as weeks: (gdb) p 0xffffffffffffffffULL/(60*60*24*7) $2 = 30500568904943 That's 14 chars plus NUL, not 11 chars plus NUL. Expand the buffer to 16 chars. I think the unpatched code apparently works if the stack-protector is not enabled because on a 32-bit machine the buffer won't be overflowed and on a 64-bit machine there's a 64-bit aligned pointer at one side and an int that isn't checked again on the other side. The panic incurred looks something like: Kernel panic - not syncing: stack-protector: Kernel stack is corrupted in: ffffffff81352ebe CPU: 0 PID: 1692 Comm: reproducer Not tainted 4.7.2-201.fc24.x86_64 #1 Hardware name: Red Hat KVM, BIOS 0.5.1 01/01/2011 0000000000000086 00000000fbbd2679 ffff8800a044bc00 ffffffff813d941f ffffffff81a28d58 ffff8800a044bc98 ffff8800a044bc88 ffffffff811b2cb6 ffff880000000010 ffff8800a044bc98 ffff8800a044bc30 00000000fbbd2679 Call Trace: [<ffffffff813d941f>] dump_stack+0x63/0x84 [<ffffffff811b2cb6>] panic+0xde/0x22a [<ffffffff81352ebe>] ? proc_keys_show+0x3ce/0x3d0 [<ffffffff8109f7f9>] __stack_chk_fail+0x19/0x30 [<ffffffff81352ebe>] proc_keys_show+0x3ce/0x3d0 [<ffffffff81350410>] ? key_validate+0x50/0x50 [<ffffffff8134db30>] ? key_default_cmp+0x20/0x20 [<ffffffff8126b31c>] seq_read+0x2cc/0x390 [<ffffffff812b6b12>] proc_reg_read+0x42/0x70 [<ffffffff81244fc7>] __vfs_read+0x37/0x150 [<ffffffff81357020>] ? security_file_permission+0xa0/0xc0 [<ffffffff81246156>] vfs_read+0x96/0x130 [<ffffffff81247635>] SyS_read+0x55/0xc0 [<ffffffff817eb872>] entry_SYSCALL_64_fastpath+0x1a/0xa4 Reported-by: Ondrej Kozina <okozina@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com> Tested-by: Ondrej Kozina <okozina@redhat.com> cc: stable@vger.kernel.org Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.l.morris@oracle.com> (cherry picked from commit 03dab869b7b239c4e013ec82aea22e181e441cfc) BUG=b:33006021, chromium:679485 TEST=kernel compiles Change-Id: Id945e0d89cb53a35eb6add597681fdb3ad045de8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/413000 Commit-Ready: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Tested-by: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit f707658635bb9d9887e213b58da9c263c08a98c8) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/426095 Commit-Ready: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Tested-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>
